chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The five-year contract, her salary and expenses
summary: She earned about $750 at the club with weekly expenses withheld, and Claude had no business sense.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Was there a time limit on your

A five year contract. But, things began happening so fast, and as I said before, Claude couldn't do anything. He had gone as far as he could go. So an Attorney, John Glespin approached me and signed me up with Columbia Artists. And of course they knew what my situation was with Claude and Gladys, and so they relinquished part of their commission which they were to receive to be held in escrow in lieu of a settlement with Gladys and Claude. And so for the next five years a certain amount of mine, in fact, when I finally got out to Hollywood, you know, this trip to Hollywood, to go out and work in a Club there. When I got out to the Versailles on the Strip there, there was a wire there from Gladys Mosier asking the management to hold my salary. So from then on for the next five years I received a certain amount of salary and the rest was held in escrow in lieu of the settlement.
Can I ask approximately how large a salary would be in those days?
Well, in the Club my salary was like $750. But I was getting a $150 and all of my
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
expenses taken care of. I had no idea of what was being withheld for the settlement. I was quite . . .
That was for a period of a week?

Yeah, a week. And of course I worked in the Club and I later went out there and did the movie. And if I wanted anything, you know, if I needed things for my performance I could always get it against the account, the escrow account. And I was a little upset because it created an estrangement between Claude and me that I didn't particularly appreciate so much. I believe it was Gladys who probably started the litigation or whatever you want to call it, and naturally Claude had to go along for the ride. But then we became, I suppose between the attorney and the management at Columbia, they weren't going to just let them - there's a certain procedure I suppose, you know, I mean let them just put a claim on my salary. They had to produce something. So the arrangement with Claude was, he was supposed to provide me with X-number of arrangements a year which probably annoyed him because by this time he had to get an attorney to take up his case, and I suppose he said that if he was going to do these arrangements

The first year or so after the procedure began he showed up and I think he did one date out in California where he got a group together, and then after that began to drift apart. ...Alec

Yeah, Wilder and then Lou Singer and different arrangers. I didn't realize what was happening. I expected the relationship to continue the way it always had but there was no way. You get a divorce from somebody you just don't . . .
